7.8.2.1 Authenticity of QSEvs
IdsM can optionally protect the authenticity of QSEvs using cryptographic authenticator generated by the Csm in conjunction with the crypto stack. It can be used to ensure authenticity as well as to prove integrity of messages from the IdsM via all communication systems until reaching the Backend or SOC (End2End-Security).
[SWS_IdsM_01204] Authenticating QSEv Upstream requirements: RS_Ids_00505, RS_Ids_00630
⌈The IdsM shall be able to attach a cryptographic authenticator, with the same data format, to each QSEv. The authentication feature is optional and shall be activated or deactivated globally for all QSEvs by setting the parameter IdsMAuthenticatorSupport to TRUE or FALSE.⌋
[SWS_IdsM_01205] AuthenticatorLength Upstream requirements: RS_Ids_00505, RS_Ids_00630
⌈The IdsM’s parameter IdsMAuthenticatorLength shall define the length in bytes of the authenticator calculated by the crypto services. It shall be configured when the authentication feature is activated.⌋ The IdsM’s Csm Job IdsMCsmJobReference has two different types of authentication processing: synchronous and asynchronous. This processing is configured in the Csm Job Primitive linked to the Csm Job, and determines the internal handling of the IdsM for the authentication.
[SWS_IdsM_01206] GenerateAuthenticator Upstream requirements: RS_Ids_00505, RS_Ids_00630
⌈In order to generate an authenticator by a Csm job IdsMCsmJobReference, the authentication generation shall be triggered by calling the Csm function Csm_ SignatureGenerate or Csm_MacGenerate depending on the selected IdsMAuthenticatorType.⌋ Manager
[SWS_IdsM_01207] SynchronousAuthenticatorGeneration Upstream requirements: RS_Ids_00505, RS_Ids_00630
⌈If the authenticator is generated by a synchronous Csm job IdsMCsmJobReference, when the function Csm_SignatureGenerate or Csm_MacGenerate returns, the authenticator shall be immediately available.⌋
